payout_quote: Anyone can sign up to be a researcher. To become a researcher, you need to create an account. Researchers can participate in any public bounty program that we run.
steps: Create a free Bugcrowd researcher account.
Read Bugcrowd's code of conduct and standard disclosure terms before starting.
Browse public bounty programs and review each program's rules and scope.
Perform authorized testing within scope and submit vulnerability reports.
Valid submissions earn points (reputation/leaderboard) and monetary bounties from the program owner, plus occasional swag.
catches: Only valid submissions earn rewards — duplicates and out-of-scope reports earn nothing.
Bounty amounts are set per program; no platform-wide payout range.
Private programs may require identity verification before participation.
Requires real security skills; beginners earn nothing for a long time.
Strict rules of engagement: violating scope can end your researcher account.
biggest_catch: Payment requires valid, unique, in-scope findings — the vast majority of time spent testing yields no payout.
eligibility: Free account open to anyone; public programs need no invitation.
timing: Programs run continuously; rewards paid per program terms after validation.

c1.evidence: Bugcrowd's own researcher docs state: 'Anyone can sign up to be a researcher... Researchers can participate in any public bounty program that we run' and rewards are 'Monetary: Financial compensation that you receive from a company when you submit a valid vulnerability.'

c2.evidence: Official terms tie monetary rewards to valid vulnerabilities per program — amounts are program-set; framed as variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official flow: create account, read rules, join public programs, test in scope, submit reports.

c4.evidence: Joining and participating are free; no upfront fee documented.

s2.note: Framed as variable per-program bounties; no fixed amount promised.

s3.note: Catches cover duplicate/out-of-scope non-payment and skill requirements.

s4.note: Deduped: no Bugcrowd route in qa/existing-providers.txt, dedupe-check.py, or qa/verification/*.json.
